verses.1: So, how can we say that Abraham was our forefather by his flesh?
verses.2: For if Abraham was justified by his works, he has the glory; but not as God.
verses.3: What does the text actually say? Abraham believed in the God, and he judged him fairly.
verses.4: But to those who work, the payment is not given according to merit, but rather due to harm or disadvantage.
verses.5: And those who do not act in accordance with justice, and who believe that the unjust are right, then their faith is considered to be in line with justice.
verses.6: Just as David says, the happiness of a person is what God calls justice, regardless of any actions one may take.
verses.7: How desirable it would be if those who were innocent could be freed from their sins, and if their faults could be revealed.
verses.8: He is a great man; it’s not right for a master to ignore his sins.
verses.9: Is this then the blessing that comes with circumcision or with anal surgery? We say that Abraham’s faith led him to righteousness.
verses.10: How then did he judge? Was it in the peritoneum or in the acrosphenoid? It wasn’t in the peritoneum, but in the acrosphenoid.
verses.11: And he also received a mark of circumcision, a symbol of the righteousness of faith that resides within him. He became the father of all those who believe through circumcision. He was given the authority to judge them according to their faith.
verses.12: And the father of circumcision is not only those who are circumcised, but also those who belong to the people who follow the faith of our father Abraham.
verses.13: For it is not by law that Abraham or his seed will be considered the heir to him in this world, but by the faith of justice.
verses.14: For if those who are heirs by law do not accept the inheritance, then the trust is broken and the promise is invalidated.
verses.15: For the law causes anger; but what isn’t a law is not also a violation either.
verses.16: Therefore, out of faith, so that the message might be truly effective for all people, not only according to law, but also because of Abraham’s faith. He is the father of us all.
verses.17: As it is written that the Father of many nations was a false god; he believed in the living God, calling those who were dead “living ones”.
verses.18: He who hoped in hope, believed that he would become the father of many nations according to what was said. Thus shall your seed be.
verses.19: And not losing faith in himself, he preserved his body from being destroyed. This lasted for a hundred years. And also, the death of the queen Sára was prevented from happening.
verses.20: But in the announcement of God, faith was not lost; instead, it was strengthened. Thus, it became worthy of God’s praise.
verses.21: And having been informed that what was requested is indeed possible and can be accomplished.
verses.23: But he did not write down only that he was justified in his actions.
verses.24: But also by us: those who believe in the resurrection of our Lord Jesus from the dead.
verses.25: He was delivered through our actions, and he was honored by our rights.
